title: GA4 ecommerce events and conversion rates
summary: Connect product views, carts, checkouts and purchases into a funnel you can reconcile.
why: Funnel losses show whether to improve the product page, cart or checkout.
Inconsistent denominators, amounts and events lead to conflicting conclusions.
know: Core events include view_item_list/select_item, view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout, purchase and refund. Add shipping and payment events as needed.
Define triggers, item_id, items, value and currency. Use a stable transaction_id to match purchases and refunds to orders.
Purchase session conversion rate is sessions with a purchase divided by all sessions in the same scope. Orders per session and all-key-event rate differ.
If 100 of 10,000 sessions include a purchase, the rate is 1%. Align time zone, device, market, period and consent coverage.
GA4, Shopify and Ads have different attribution and tracking limits. Order accounting is the transaction baseline; reports need not match exactly.
inputs: Property, data stream, event sources and test environment
Product/variant ID mappings, tax and shipping value rules, de-identified test orders
actions: Define one sender per event and parameter. Check native integrations and gaps between custom storefront and hosted checkout.
Verify cross-domain source continuity; avoid self or payment-provider referrals. Do not send personal data such as email to analytics.
Check event order, values and currencies in DebugView, requests and reports. Test reloads, failed payments, refunds and consent.
Deliver a funnel and metric dictionary with numerators, denominators, test exclusions and reasons for discrepancies.
done: Reloads do not duplicate purchases; refunds match the original transaction.
Reports show funnels by channel/device and reproduce the agreed conversion rate.
pitfalls: Sending purchase on a checkout-button click or failed payment.
Calling orders divided by users a session conversion rate.
decision: Agree on purchase, revenue and conversion definitions.

reader.concept: GA4 records customer actions as events. Connecting views, carts, checkouts and purchases reveals the shopping funnel.
reader.when: Use this to inspect drop-offs, calculate conversion rates or verify purchase tracking.

example.situation: If 100 of 10,000 sessions contain a purchase, purchase session conversion is 1%.
example.lesson: State the denominator before comparing rates.

reader.first_step: Agree on what counts as a purchase and conversion before checking events.
terms: A recorded action, such as adding to cart.
A group of interactions during one visit; a user can have several.
An order identifier used to recognize the same transaction.
